segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Katrin and today we have an elementary level lesson for you.
segments.zh: 我的名字是卡特琳，今天我们为您准备了一节初级课程。

segments.en: This one is especially for people who are interested in babies.
segments.zh: 这一款特别适合对婴儿感兴趣的人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Maybe you have a baby, you will have a baby, maybe you're pregnant and this is a great lesson for that because we are talking about a baby shower.
segments.zh: 也许你有一个孩子，你即将有一个孩子，也许你怀孕了，这是一节很棒的课，因为我们要谈论的是婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: Okay, so before we get started, let's take a look at vocabulary preview and learn what exactly a baby shower is.
segments.zh: 好吧，在我们开始之前，让我们看看词汇预览，了解婴儿送礼会到底是什么。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预览。

segments.en: Okay, so a baby shower.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: You would think that this is about bathing the baby, about giving the baby a bath.
segments.zh: 你会认为这是关于给宝宝洗澡，给宝宝洗澡。

segments.en: No, not a real shower.
segments.zh: 不，不是真正的淋浴。

segments.en: A baby shower or a bridal shower, these are parties.
segments.zh: 婴儿送礼会或新娘送礼会，这些都是派对。

segments.en: Okay, they're parties.
segments.zh: 好吧，他们是派对。

segments.en: And in this case, a baby shower is a party that you throw for a woman that is pregnant, right?
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，婴儿送礼会是你为准妈妈举办的派对，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if my sister is going to have a baby, I throw her a baby shower.
segments.zh: 所以如果我姐姐要生孩子，我会给她办个婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: It's a party where all of her friends give her gifts.
segments.zh: 这是一个她所有的朋友都给她礼物的聚会。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Yeah, it's a way to celebrate having a baby.
segments.zh: 是的，这是庆祝生孩子的一种方式。

segments.en: Okay, so they give her gifts, you'll play games as well as to like maybe guess the name of the baby or guess the sex of the baby.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以他们给她礼物，你会玩游戏以及喜欢猜猜婴儿的名字或猜测婴儿的性别。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Stuff like that.
segments.zh: 诸如此类的东西。

segments.en: Okay, so it's a very common thing.
segments.zh: 好的，所以这是一个非常常见的事情。

segments.en: I think it's mostly for women.
segments.zh: 我认为主要是针对女性的。

segments.en: I don't really know if men have baby showers as well.
segments.zh: 我真的不知道男人是否也会办婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: I don't think so.
segments.zh: 我不这么认为。

segments.en: I don't think so either.
segments.zh: 我也不这么认为。

segments.en: But it's a very popular tradition in the United States and many other parts of the world.
segments.zh: 但它在美国和世界许多其他地区是一个非常流行的传统。

segments.en: So we're going to talk about that.
segments.zh: 所以我们要谈谈这个。

segments.en: Let's listen to the dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: 让我们第一次听对话。

segments.en: Thank you for organizing this great baby shower for me.
segments.zh: 感谢您为我组织了这个精彩的婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: I've always been to baby showers but never actually had one held for me.
segments.zh: 我参加过不少准妈妈派对，但这还是头一次别人专门为我办。

segments.en: Let's get started.
segments.zh: 我们开始吧。

segments.en: Okay, let's start opening some presents.
segments.zh: 好的，让我们开始打开一些礼物。

segments.en: Oh, look, what a great little bib for the baby.
segments.zh: 哦，看，这对宝宝来说是多么棒的小围兜。

segments.en: This will definitely come in handy.
segments.zh: 这肯定会派上用场。

segments.en: Oh, wow, you also got me a stroller.
segments.zh: 哦，哇，你也给我买了一辆婴儿车。

segments.en: That's so great.
segments.zh: 真是太好了。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: This next one is from Betty.
segments.zh: 下一份是贝蒂送的。

segments.en: A high chair and a car seat.
segments.zh: 一把宝宝餐椅和一个儿童汽车安全座椅。

segments.en: Wow, Betty, thank you so much.
segments.zh: 哇，贝蒂，非常感谢。

segments.en: I really appreciate it.
segments.zh: 我真的很感激。

segments.en: One more from Carla.
segments.zh: 还有一份是卡拉送的。

segments.en: A playpen and crib.
segments.zh: 一个婴儿游戏围栏和一张婴儿床。

segments.en: Thanks, Carla.
segments.zh: 谢谢，卡拉。

segments.en: This is just what I needed.
segments.zh: 这正是我所需要的。

segments.en: Okay, that's all of them.
segments.zh: 好吧，就这些了。

segments.en: No more gifts.
segments.zh: 没有别的礼物了。

segments.en: Now who wants to guess when the baby is due?
segments.zh: 现在谁来猜猜宝宝什么时候出生？

segments.en: I think my water just broke.
segments.zh: 我的羊水好像破了。

segments.en: Get me to a hospital.
segments.zh: 送我去医院。

segments.en: All right, so very interesting.
segments.zh: 好吧，非常有趣。

segments.en: All the gifts that they got and definitely very useful because this is a very common items that you get for babies, right?
segments.zh: 他们收到的所有礼物，绝对非常有用，因为这些都是给宝宝准备的常见物品，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: This stuff is really, really valuable because if you have a baby or if your brother or sister has a baby, you'll notice that these are very common items.
segments.zh: 这些东西真的非常有价值，因为如果你有一个孩子或者你的兄弟姐妹有一个孩子，你会注意到这些是非常常见的物品。

segments.en: So let's go through a couple of them in today's Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 因此，让我们在今天的语言要点中介绍其中的一些内容。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay, so the first word that we're going to take a look at, the most common one and useful one for a baby is a bib.
segments.zh: 好的，我们要看的第一个词，对婴儿最常见和最有用的词是围兜。

segments.en: Bib.
segments.zh: 围兜。

segments.en: So, babies are messy.
segments.zh: 所以，宝宝很乱。

segments.en: When they eat food, they get their food on their clothes.
segments.zh: 他们吃东西时，食物会弄到衣服上。

segments.en: So to protect the clothes, babies wear bibs.
segments.zh: 所以为了保护衣服，宝宝们会穿围兜。

segments.en: This is a piece of cloth or fabric around their neck.
segments.zh: 这是他们脖子上的一块布或织物。

segments.en: Okay, a bib.
segments.zh: 好吧，围兜。

segments.en: And also, sometimes you want to go out with your baby to the mall, you're walking and you don't want to carry him in your arms all the time.
segments.zh: 而且，有时你想和你的宝宝一起去商场，你在走路，你不想一直把他抱在怀里。

segments.en: So you need a stroller.
segments.zh: 所以你需要一个婴儿车。

segments.en: Okay, so basically a stroller is a chair on wheels for a baby.
segments.zh: 好的，所以婴儿车基本上就是带轮子的婴儿座椅。

segments.en: Babies are heavy and as they get older, they get heavier.
segments.zh: 婴儿很重，随着年龄的增长，他们变得更重。

segments.en: And so this is a way to push the baby around, not carry the baby.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种推婴儿的方式，而不是抱婴儿。

segments.en: Right, and maybe the baby falls asleep, so they can fall asleep in the stroller.
segments.zh: 对，也许婴儿睡着了，这样他们就可以在婴儿车里睡着了。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay, and while talking about chairs, we're going to take a look at two different types of chairs.
segments.zh: 好的，在谈论椅子时，我们将看看两种不同类型的椅子。

segments.en: First one is a high chair.
segments.zh: 第一个是高脚椅。

segments.en: Okay, high chair.
segments.zh: 好吧，高脚椅。

segments.en: Think about the word high, that means tall in this case.
segments.zh: 想想 high 这个词，在这里就是“高”的意思。

segments.en: A high chair is a chair for babies at the table.
segments.zh: 高脚椅是让宝宝在餐桌旁用的椅子。

segments.en: So if you put a baby on a regular chair, they can't eat with adults.
segments.zh: 所以如果你把婴儿放在普通椅子上，他们不能和成年人一起吃饭。

segments.en: Right, they're too small.
segments.zh: 对，他们太小了。

segments.en: So we give them high chairs so that they can sit a little bit higher and they can be at the table with adults.
segments.zh: 所以我们给他们高脚椅，这样他们就可以坐得更高一点，他们可以和成年人一起坐在桌子旁。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So they're very common.
segments.zh: 所以它们很常见。

segments.en: For example, you go to a restaurant, they will have a little high chairs if you have a baby or a small child.
segments.zh: 例如，你去一家餐馆，如果你有一个孩子或一个小孩，他们会有一张高脚椅。

segments.en: So if you're at a restaurant, you have a baby, you ask for a high chair.
segments.zh: 所以如果你在餐馆，你有一个婴儿，你要一张高脚椅。

segments.en: You say, do you have a high chair, please?
segments.zh: 你说，请问你有高脚椅吗？

segments.en: Yeah, perfect.
segments.zh: 是的，完美。

segments.en: And well, if you're going to the restaurant or you go anywhere in your car, you need to have the baby be safe and obviously they can't fit on a normal seat.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你要去餐厅，或者开车去别的地方，你需要保证宝宝的安全，显然他们没法坐在普通座位上。

segments.en: No, with a seat belt?
segments.zh: 不，带安全带？

segments.en: No, I don't think so.
segments.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

segments.en: So that's why you get them a car seat.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么你给他们一个汽车座椅。

segments.en: Okay, a car seat is a special chair that goes on the seat of the car and usually it's very, very safe.
segments.zh: 好的，汽车座椅是放在汽车座位上的特殊座椅，通常非常非常安全。

segments.en: It's made to protect the baby.
segments.zh: 它是为了保护宝宝而设计的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So if you are ever in a car accident, the car seat will help protect the small baby.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您遇到过车祸，汽车座椅将有助于保护小婴儿。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's supposed to go in the back of the car, not the front.
segments.zh: 所以它应该放在汽车的后部，而不是前面。

segments.en: Yes, always.
segments.zh: 是的，总是。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And now moving on to our last two words.
segments.zh: 现在继续我们的最后两个词。

segments.en: If you're at home, you sometimes want to have the baby play and you get them a play pen.
segments.zh: 如果你在家里，有时想让宝宝玩耍，就会给他们一个游戏围栏。

segments.en: So basically this is a way for parents to leave the baby playing but not look at the baby the whole time.
segments.zh: 所以基本上这是父母让宝宝玩耍的一种方式，但不要一直看婴儿。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: A play pen is like a cage for a baby, but it's soft and it's cute and it's pretty.
segments.zh: 游戏围栏就像婴儿的笼子，但它很柔软，很可爱，很漂亮。

segments.en: So it's basically like an open area that's protected on the sides and the baby can go inside but the baby can't leave.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上就像一个侧面受到保护的开放区域，婴儿可以进入，但宝宝不能离开。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's like a cage basically and it has little toys and that's the way you just keep them in there for a while.
segments.zh: 它基本上就像一个笼子，它有小玩具，这就是你把它们放在里面一段时间的方式。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And now when you want to put the baby to sleep, it can't obviously sleep in a big bed because it might roll over, it might fall off.
segments.zh: 现在当你想让宝宝睡觉时，宝宝显然不能睡在大床上，因为他可能会翻身，可能会掉下来。

segments.en: There's a lot of things that can go wrong, so you get them a crib.
segments.zh: 有很多事情可能会出错，所以你给他们一个婴儿床。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So a crib is a bed for babies.
segments.zh: 所以婴儿床是婴儿的床。

segments.en: This is usually high off the ground and it's usually quite small and the baby can't climb out of it.
segments.zh: 这通常离地面很高，而且通常很小，宝宝不能爬出来。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's a very safe bed so the baby can't fall out, can't climb out.
segments.zh: 所以这是一张非常安全的床，所以宝宝不能掉出来，不能爬出来。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So very interesting, very useful things for you if you're having a baby, planning on getting these things.
segments.zh: 如果您要生孩子，计划获得这些东西，这对您来说非常有趣、非常有用。

segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不回去，再听一次对话，我们会带着流利表达回来。

segments.zh: 我参加过不少准妈妈派对，但这还是头一次别人专门为我办。

segments.zh: 我们开始吧。

segments.en: This will definitely come in handy.
segments.zh: 这肯定会派上用场。

segments.en: Oh wow, you also got me a stroller.
segments.zh: 哦，哇，你也给我买了一辆婴儿车。

segments.en: That's so great.
segments.zh: 真是太好了。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: Wow, Betty, thank you so much.
segments.zh: 哇，贝蒂，非常感谢。

segments.zh: 我真的很感激。

segments.en: One more from Carla.
segments.zh: 还有一份是卡拉送的。

segments.en: A playpen and crib.
segments.zh: 一个婴儿游戏围栏和一张婴儿床。

segments.en: Thanks, Carla.
segments.zh: 谢谢，卡拉。

segments.en: This is just what I needed.
segments.zh: 这正是我所需要的。

segments.en: Okay, that's all of them.
segments.zh: 好吧，就这些了。

segments.en: No more gifts.
segments.zh: 没有别的礼物了。

segments.zh: 现在谁来猜猜宝宝什么时候出生？

segments.zh: 我想我的羊水刚破了。

segments.zh: 送我去医院。

segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at two key phrases.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看两个关键短语。

segments.en: Easy Builder.
segments.zh: Easy Builder.

segments.en: Okay, so at the beginning of the dialogue, the woman receives a bib for the baby and she says, this will definitely come in handy.
segments.zh: 好的，所以在对话开始时，女人会为婴儿收到一个围兜，她说，这肯定会派上用场。

segments.en: To come in handy.
segments.zh: 派上用场。

segments.en: Right, so when something comes in handy, it means it will be useful.
segments.zh: 是的，所以当某些东西派上用场时，这意味着它会很有用。

segments.en: Okay, so something that's handy is useful.
segments.zh: 好的，所以方便的东西很有用。

segments.en: To come in handy means to be useful.
segments.zh: 派上用场意味着有用。

segments.en: It will be useful in the future.
segments.zh: 将来会很有用。

segments.en: So for example, you should take a flashlight with you in the car just in case because it could come in handy.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，您应该在车内随身携带一个手电筒，以防万一，因为它可能会派上用场。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Or if I know that Marco is traveling to India, I can give him a map of India.
segments.zh: 或者，如果我知道马可要去印度旅行，我可以给他一张印度的地图。

segments.en: I say, Marco, this map might come in handy.
segments.zh: 我说，马可，这张地图可能会派上用场。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So to come in handy or in something that is handy, something that's useful.
segments.zh: 所以派上用场或有用的东西，有用的东西。

segments.en: And towards the end, a very popular phrase you probably heard in every movie that has like maybe a pregnant woman in there.
segments.zh: 到最后，还有一句很流行的话，你可能在每部有孕妇的电影里都听过。

segments.en: My water just broke.
segments.zh: 我的羊水刚破了。

segments.en: My water broke.
segments.zh: 我的羊水破了。

segments.en: Okay, so the woman says, my water broke.
segments.zh: 好吧，女人说，我的水破了。

segments.en: Take me to the hospital.
segments.zh: 带我去医院。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Okay, so this means I'm having my baby right now.
segments.zh: 好的，这意味着我现在要生孩子了。

segments.en: So why do they say that the water broke?
segments.zh: 那么为什么他们说水破了呢？

segments.en: Because actually water kind of breaks, right?
segments.zh: 因为实际上羊水确实会破，对吧？

segments.en: I think there's a protective water cushion.
segments.zh: 我认为有一个保护性水垫。

segments.en: Basically there's a sack of water protecting the baby.
segments.zh: 基本上有一袋水保护婴儿。

segments.en: It's not just water.
segments.zh: 这不仅仅是水。

segments.en: It's all sorts of like body fluids.
segments.zh: 它就像各种体液一样。

segments.en: And basically when that breaks, it comes out and you know that you're going to have the baby because that means the baby has to come out now because that protective fluid is gone.
segments.zh: 基本上，当它破裂时，它会出来，你知道你会生孩子，因为这意味着婴儿现在必须出来，因为保护液已经消失了。

segments.en: Maybe the baby just kind of kicks that water out and just like, I'm ready to come out.
segments.zh: 也许宝宝只是把水踢掉了，就像，我准备出来了。

segments.en: I have no idea how it works.
segments.zh: 我不知道它是如何工作的。

segments.en: All right, so very interesting stuff.
segments.zh: 好吧，非常有趣的东西。

segments.zh: 感谢您为我组织了这个精彩的婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: I've always been to baby showers but never actually had one held for me.
segments.zh: 我参加过不少准妈妈派对，但这还是头一次别人专门为我办。

segments.en: Let's get started.
segments.zh: 我们开始吧。

segments.en: Okay, let's start opening some presents.
segments.zh: 好的，让我们开始打开一些礼物。

segments.en: Oh look, what a great little bib for the baby.
segments.zh: 哦，看，这对宝宝来说是多么棒的小围兜。

segments.en: This will definitely come in handy.
segments.zh: 这肯定会派上用场。

segments.en: Oh wow, you also got me a stroller.
segments.zh: 哦，哇，你也给我买了一辆婴儿车。

segments.en: That's so great.
segments.zh: 真是太好了。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: This next one is from Betty.
segments.zh: 下一份是贝蒂送的。

segments.en: A high chair and a car seat.
segments.zh: 一把宝宝餐椅和一个儿童汽车安全座椅。

segments.en: Wow, Betty, thank you so much.
segments.zh: 哇，贝蒂，非常感谢。

segments.en: I really appreciate it.
segments.zh: 我真的很感激。

segments.en: One more from Carla.
segments.zh: 还有一份是卡拉送的。

segments.en: A playpen and crib.
segments.zh: 一个婴儿游戏围栏和一张婴儿床。

segments.en: Thanks Carla.
segments.zh: 谢谢卡拉。

segments.en: That's just what I needed.
segments.zh: 这正是我所需要的。

segments.en: Okay, that's all of them.
segments.zh: 好吧，就这些了。

segments.en: No more gifts.
segments.zh: 没有别的礼物了。

segments.en: Now who wants to guess when the baby is due?
segments.zh: 现在谁来猜猜宝宝什么时候出生？

segments.en: I think my water just broke.
segments.zh: 我想我的羊水刚破了。

segments.en: Get me to a hospital.
segments.zh: 送我去医院。

segments.en: All right, so talking about baby things and baby showers.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们聊了聊婴儿用品和婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: It's a very interesting tradition.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的传统。

segments.en: I understand that in other countries they don't really celebrate baby showers like this.
segments.zh: 我知道在其他国家，他们并没有真正庆祝这样的婴儿送礼会。

segments.en: Really?
segments.zh: 真的吗？

segments.en: Yeah, or that if they do, they do it in different ways.
segments.zh: 是的，或者如果他们这样做，他们以不同的方式进行。

segments.en: I know for example that sometimes in Latin American countries, they usually do it after the baby's born.
segments.zh: 例如，我知道有时在拉丁美洲国家，他们通常在婴儿出生后这样做。

segments.en: Oh, so like a congratulations shower.
segments.zh: 哦，就像祝贺性质的送礼会一样。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And then obviously you know if the baby was a boy or a girl, so then you get them like pink things or blue things.
segments.zh: 然后你显然已经知道宝宝是男孩还是女孩，所以会送粉色或蓝色的东西。

segments.en: So it's a little bit more.
segments.zh: 所以它有点多一点。

segments.en: That's what's really funny about these.
segments.zh: 这就是这些真正有趣的地方。

segments.en: People often want to have the surprise of not knowing if the baby will be a boy or a girl.
segments.zh: 人们常常想要保留那份不知道宝宝是男孩还是女孩的惊喜。

segments.en: So when they have the baby shower, they say, oh, I don't know what the gender is.
segments.zh: 所以当他们办婴儿送礼会时，他们会说，哦，我不知道宝宝的性别。

segments.en: And so you end up buying all of these yellow things because yellow is neutral.
segments.zh: 所以你最终买了所有这些黄色的东西，因为黄色是中性的。

segments.en: It's good for boys and girls.
segments.zh: 这对男孩和女孩都有好处。

segments.en: I don't know how many yellow gifts I've got.
segments.zh: 我不知道我有多少黄色礼物。

segments.en: I think it's a very interesting thing because for example, I know that in China, I think you can't ask the doctor for the gender of the baby before it's born, right?
segments.zh: 我认为这是一件非常有趣的事情，因为例如，我知道在中国，我认为您不能在婴儿出生之前向医生询问婴儿的性别，对吧？

segments.en: I think that's a way to, I'm not sure if it's a rule or not, but it sounds right.
segments.zh: 我认为这是一种方式，我不确定它是否是规则，但听起来是对的。

segments.en: I mean, it's a way to protect female babies.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种保护女婴的方式。

segments.en: I think it would be always great to just have it be a surprise.
segments.zh: 我认为让它成为一个惊喜总是很棒的。

segments.en: You never know.
segments.zh: 你永远不知道。

segments.en: Yeah, just like, oh, you know, whatever comes out.
segments.zh: 是的，就像，哦，你知道，无论结果如何。

segments.en: Can you imagine not knowing and then you have twins?
segments.zh: 你能想象不知道然后你有双胞胎吗？

segments.en: That would be great for me, I think, if I had like a boy and a girl, bam, all at once.
segments.zh: 我想，如果我同时拥有一个男孩和一个女孩，Bam，那对我来说会很棒。

segments.en: All at once, never have to worry about it again.
segments.zh: 一下子，再也不用担心了。

segments.en: Exactly, and then you have the best of both worlds, right?
segments.zh: 没错，然后你就拥有了两全其美，对吧？

segments.en: You're done.
segments.zh: 你完成了。

segments.en: All right, so very interesting topic.
segments.zh: 好吧，非常有趣的话题。

segments.en: Let us know if you have baby showers in your country or how do you celebrate a baby's birth or before it's born?
segments.zh: 告诉我们，你们国家有没有婴儿送礼会，或者你们会怎样庆祝宝宝的出生，或是在出生之前？

segments.en: What do you do?
segments.zh: 你们会怎么做呢？

segments.en: Very good question.
segments.zh: 非常好的问题。

segments.en: Let us know.
segments.zh: 告诉我们吧。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: We hope to see you there.
segments.zh: 希望到时候见到你。

segments.en: All right, bye.
segments.zh: 好，再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
